paragraphs: Four fostering services list Ealing as an area they cover: the council's own service, Ealing Fostering Connections, and three independent agencies, all shown above. Fostering for the council means caring for Ealing's own children, with the council's social workers supporting you; an agency assesses, approves and supervises its own carers and looks after children placed with it by councils. New enquiries to the council go through Foster with West London, the recruitment hub shared by eight west London councils, so one conversation covers Ealing and its neighbours.

Ealing's sufficiency strategy for 2025 to 2028 explains why the council wants more carers of its own. It looked after 280 children in September 2024, 8% fewer than a year before. In August 2024, 56 children lived with the council's own foster carers and 98 with independent agency carers, and the number of approved mainstream council fostering households fell by 14% between 2020 and 2024. Distance matters too: 61% of children with the council's carers lived inside the borough, against 11% of those living with agency carers. The council's aim is to significantly increase its own approved carers, and the homes it names as most in demand are those for brothers and sisters, teenagers, unaccompanied asylum-seeking children, and parents with their babies.

On pay, Ealing's cabinet agreed an 18.5% increase in its foster carers' allowances in October 2024. The council pages we read give no weekly figures, and we do not yet have an Ealing allowance page, so ask the council and each agency for their current rates in writing. The council's offer to its own carers also includes full council tax exemption for eligible carers, free parking in pay and display and residents' bays, discounted leisure, free green waste collection, therapeutic support from its clinical psychology service, an out-of-hours support team, ongoing training and the Mockingbird family model. Ealing was approved as a Fostering Friendly borough in September 2024.

Its recruitment advert also asks for carers for babies, school-age children and children with additional needs and disabilities, and the council works with a partner to find weekend carers who offer short breaks. Compare the council with two or three of the agencies above, and look at the Brent, Harrow, Hounslow and London pages for more services nearby.
